outlooks.summary: The main severe-weather threat for today now appears to be damaging gusts from parts of northern Iowa and southern Minnesota toward the southern Lake Michigan area. Isolated large hail also is possible in that corridor. Otherwise, severe hail and gusts may occur from afternoon and early evening storms over parts of the High Plains.

sections.title: Synopsis
sections.text: The upper-air pattern will be characterized by synoptic-scale troughing moving eastward across the western U.S., and a ridge with associated anticyclonic flow aloft shifting eastward from the Mississippi Valley region across the Great Lakes and central/southern Appalachians. As a compact mid/upper-level cyclone digs southeastward along the AK Panhandle and BC coasts, heights will fall across the Pacific Northwest. Farther southeast, a strong, basal shortwave trough -- now evident in moisture-channel imagery over CA, will move eastward across the Sierra to the NV/UT border and lower CO River Valley by the end of the period. Downstream, a broad fetch of southwesterly flow aloft will cover the Rockies and Great plains, becoming westerly over the Upper Great Lakes around the ridge. At the surface, a weak lee-side/frontal-wave low was analyzed at 11Z over southwestern NE, with a warm front northeastward over northwestern IA then southeastward across central portions of IL/IN. A dryline extended from the low near the KS/CO and TX/NM borders, to the Trans-Pecos of west TX. sections.title: MN/IA to Lake Michigan region
sections.text: A complex of scattered to numerous thunderstorms, offering damaging wind and isolated large hail, is expected to move eastward to east-southeastward across the outlook area through the afternoon. This likely will evolve from an existing area of thunderstorms currently supported by elevated inflow north of the warm front -- yet with a low-level cold pool, surface wind perturbations, and surface isallobaric rise/fall couplet already evident across portions of southern SD and extreme northern NE. Forecast MCS motion vectors suggest that the associated low/middle-level UVV field and expanding convective regime, perhaps enhanced by an MCV, will track eastward across the southern MN/northern IA area through early afternoon, encountering then straddling the warm front. The complex then may turn somewhat rightward through the upper ridge toward the southern WI/northern IL area later this afternoon and perhaps into this evening, before outrunning its most favorable instability and weakening. sections.title: Central/southern High Plains
sections.text: Despite the lack of substantial upper support, thunderstorms should develop again today near the dryline, a few of which may become high-based supercells. Activity will pose the risks of damaging gusts and large hail. With somewhat greater low-level moisture and mid/upper-level flow than the previous day, overall storm coverage, organization and intensity may be correspondingly greater, with somewhat more eastward survival into evening stabilization before weakening. As such, 15%/slight-risk probabilities are maintained. Surface dew points generally in the 50s F along the dryline (with low 60s a short distance east), vertically juxtaposed with steep lapse rates characteristic of the EML, will yield MLCAPE in the 1500-2500 J/kg range. A very well-mixed subcloud layer will support damaging gusts, and large hail also is likely from any cells exhibiting at least short-lived supercellular morphologies. Isolated significant/damaging hail and/or significant gusts are possible as well. However, any more specific focus for that aside from the broader dryline regime appears too nebulous/uncertain to draw a specific 10%/sig area within the broader hail probabilities at this time.

sections.title: Northern High Plains
sections.text: Widely scattered thunderstorms may develop this afternoon over higher terrain near the western rim of the outlook and move eastward to northeastward, with the potential for isolated large hail and severe gusts. Effective-shear magnitudes exceeding 50 kt are possible over this region, and at least an isolated supercell or two appears probable. The main uncertainties precluding greater, more focused probabilities currently involve coverage of severe potential and robustness of theta-e in trajectories in the wake of a good deal of morning convection to the southeast over SD/NE. ..Edwards/Peters.. 05/15/2017

outlooks.summary: Thunderstorms will impact parts of the Upper Midwest and high Plains this afternoon through tonight, accompanied by a risk for severe weather. This may include at least some potential for a couple of tornadoes, but severe hail and wind appear the primary severe threats.

sections.title: Synopsis
sections.text: Mid/upper troughing, with an embedded closed low, is forecast to pivot inland across southern California, and take on an increasing negative tilt orientation across the southern Great Basin/Colorado Valley region by late tonight, as another vigorous upper impulse/closed low dig into the Pacific Northwest. Downstream, large-scale mid/upper ridging appears likely to remain prominent east of the Rockies, through the lower Great Lakes region and Appalachians. Weak to modest mid-level height falls may occur across much of the Rockies through the northern half of the Plains by late tonight in response to progression of the upstream perturbations, but models suggest that mid/upper flow, while at least modestly strong, will remain broadly anticyclonic. Still, beneath increasingly divergent upper flow between a couple of mid/upper jet streaks (one rounding the crest of the ridging and the other within the base of Southwestern troughing), a consolidating and deepening surface low seems likely to emerge within lee surface troughing across parts of western into central South Dakota and Nebraska by late tonight. sections.title: Upper Midwest
sections.text: Forcing for ascent supporting an ongoing area of thunderstorms spreading northeast of the mid Missouri Valley appears largely in mid-levels, associated with a weak perturbation rounding the crest of the larger-scale ridging, which may build further northward across much of the region through the day. Given the large potential instability now evolving across the mid Missouri Valley, supported by a combination of modest low-level moisture and very steep mid-level lapse rates, there does appear at least considerable conditional severe weather potential in the wake of this activity. However, in the presence of larger-scale mid-level height rises and generally weak low-level forcing for storm development, convective potential remains unclear through at least the daytime hours. And it is not clear that convection allowing model guidance is handling this well. sections.title: Central and southern high Plains
sections.text: Model output continues to indicate the initiation of considerable thunderstorm activity in the peak late afternoon surface heating near/east of the lee surface trough, particularly from portions of the Texas Panhandle into western Kansas. In the presence of thermodynamic profiles characterized by a modestly moist and deeply mixed boundary layer and steep lower/mid tropospheric lapse rates, coupled with 30-40 kt southwesterly lower/mid tropospheric flow, the environment appears conducive to storms capable of producing severe hail and wind gusts.

sections.title: Northern high Plains
sections.text: Strengthening vertical shear and destabilization within southeasterly low-level flow across the Black Hills region into northeastern Wyoming and southeastern Montana probably will become sufficient to support a few severe storms, including isolated supercells, late this afternoon and evening. ..Kerr/Dean.. 05/15/2017

sections.title: 20Z Outlook Discussion
sections.text: The only notable change to the ongoing forecast has been a westward adjustment of the Marginal delineation across parts of southwest NE, eastward CO, and vicinity. Ascent accompanying a weak midlevel impulse glancing the western extent of Gulf moisture over the Great Plains may support isolated storms capable of severe hail/wind within areas added to Marginal designation. Otherwise, no changes have been made to the ongoing forecast. ..Cohen.. 05/15/2017 .PREV DISCUSSION... /ISSUED 1127 AM CDT Mon May 15 2017/

outlooks.summary: Severe storms with damaging wind and hail are expected from northeast Iowa across parts of southern Wisconsin and northern Illinois this evening. Severe wind and hail are also expected across parts of the central and northern High Plains.

sections.title: Iowa, Southern Wisconsin, Northern Illinois
sections.text: A small, but severe MCS has formed over northern IA and is rapidly progressing eastward toward the MS river. This system contain both severe wind and hail, and is expected to maintain strength as it moves east-southeastward along a warm front into southern WI and northern IL later this evening. These storms will be supported by a southwesterly feed of warm air, which will maintain lift near the front/outflow boundaries. The 00Z DVN showed steep lapse rates throughout the profile, which should help to fight against increasing CIN over the next few hours. While tornadoes are not expected to be the primary threat, a small corridor from northeastern IA into southwest WI may be favorable as shear is maximized along the warm front. For more information see MCD 0720. As for areas to the west, including southeast SD, nocturnal warm advection will increase tonight, which will enhance lift north of the front. Elevated hail will be possible, but a conditional wind threat also exists depending on how organized the cluster over NE becomes.

sections.title: Northern High Plains, Central High Plains, Texas Panhandle
sections.text: A broad low-pressure trough currently stretches from eastern WY southward into western TX with modest mid to upper level southwesterly flow overspreading the region. Low-level flow is more backed across the northern Plains, which is helping to bring moisture westward, supporting isolated supercells capable of hail or a brief/weak tornado. To the south, stronger heating has occurred from CO/KS into TX, contributing to over 1500 J/kg MLCAPE. The strong heating has also resulted in deeply mixed boundary layers, with strong surface wind gusts. The 00Z soundings from LBF, DDC and AMA all show good lapse rates aloft with veering wind profiles with height, supportive of a few supercells with hail. Radar trends suggest the hail threat is currently maximized from the TX/OK panhandles into southwest KS.

sections.title: Central/Eastern Nebraska
sections.text: A cluster of storms is currently moving from northwest KS into southern NE, with more of a cold pool and wind threat developing in addition to hail. These storms look to be spreading northeastward, and will affect much of north central KS into south central NE this evening. The 00Z OAX sounding shows impressive lapse rate profiles with only a small capping inversion below 700 MB. While some increase in CIN is expected with time, mainly to the southeast, any organized cold pool from storms to the west may eventually result in at least an isolated wind threat across the remainder of eastern NE. Therefore, have added a conditional 15% wind threat for near/after 06Z. For more information see MCD 0721. ..Jewell.. 05/16/2017

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Strong thunderstorm clusters will spread east along the MN/IA border this morning. Gusty winds and small hail are possible.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Remnants of late evening convection, that developed near the Black Hills of SD around 03z, have progressed into southeast SD where an MCV appears to have developed within an expanding cluster of thunderstorms. This activity is gradually maturing within a weakly forced low-level warm advection regime characterized by marginal instability but steep mid-level lapse rates. 12z observed soundings do not suggest the air mass ahead of this evolving MCS is particularly unstable but this cluster of storms should propagate east along the MN/IA border. Gusty winds and small hail are the primary threats and unless this activity becomes stronger than currently anticipated a WW is not warranted.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Scattered thunderstorm development is expected later this afternoon, with a threat of locally damaging wind and isolated large hail. Watch issuance is possible by 21Z.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Latest satellite imagery indicates surface-based cumulus beginning to develop over portions of west TX/TX panhandle, and also over southeast CO and far eastern NM. As strong heating continues this afternoon within a modestly moist boundary layer, deep convection is expected to initiate by 21-22Z. There are two zones of possible initiation -- one along the primary moisture gradient across far eastern NM into southeast CO, and the second further east along a low-level confluence zone noted in recent surface obs from western KS into the central TX panhandle. As storms intensify later this afternoon, moderate MLCAPE OF 1500-2000 J/kg and effective shear of 30-40 kts will be sufficient for some storm organization, with a few supercells possible. Relatively large temperature/dewpoint spreads will result in a damaging wind threat, while steep midlevel lapse rates will support a threat of severe hail with the strongest cells.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Isolated strong thunderstorms may develop across northern Iowa late this afternoon into the evening hours. Large hail and damaging winds are the primary threats. WW may be required by 23z.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Early-day MCS that moved across SD has progressed into WI aided in part by weak low-level warm advection. Short-range model guidance has struggled with this activity, likely due to weak forcing, with multiple disjointed surface boundaries possibly being influential later this evening for renewed development. Latest satellite imagery suggests a mid-level vort max may be approaching the Missouri River northwest of OMA. Ahead of this feature, mid-level convection is gradually thickening and isolated elevated thunderstorms are now evident ahead of the vort stretching into northern IA. While boundary-layer cu is focused along the southern-most outflow across central IA, there appears to be sufficient CINH across this region such that deep convection may struggle. Current thinking is deep convection will focus north of the southern-most outflow with a gradual upward trend possible into the evening hours. Hail and wind are the primary threats with this slowly evolving activity.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: A few severe thunderstorms are possible this afternoon into early evening, with a threat of large hail and locally damaging winds.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Latest WV imagery indicates a low-amplitude shortwave trough moving northeastward across UT. As this feature approaches the northern High Plains, scattered thunderstorms are expected to continue to develop across portions of eastern WY and southeast MT, with initiation focused over the high terrain and potentially along a cold front currently draped from north-central WY into southeast MT. Moist southeasterly low-level flow has allowed moderate buoyancy to develop across this region, with SB CAPE of 1200-2000 J/kg noted per recent mesoanalysis, while effective shear of 35-45 kts will support some organized storm structures, with isolated supercells possible. Steep midlevel lapse rates will support a large hail threat, with locally damaging winds also possible, especially in areas where diurnal heating has resulted in steep low-level lapse rates. Further east over western SD, persistent cloudiness has prevented substantial destabilization thus far, but initiation near the Black Hills cannot be ruled out in the next 2-3 hours, with convection developing over WY eventually impacting this area into the evening. A conditional threat of large hail will exist with any storms in this region late this afternoon into this evening. Some uncertainty remains regarding the coverage of the severe threat across the MCD area, but watch issuance is possible if a threat of multiple supercells appears imminent.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Isolated thunderstorms in the region will pose a risk of hail and gusty winds, and an isolated tornado cannot be ruled out. The severe threat should be isolated enough to preclude a WW issuance, although convective trends will be monitored.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: An isolated surface-based severe thunderstorm has developed in northern Illinois in the past hour on the southern flank of a remnant MCS that is currently weakening in Wisconsin. The surface pattern in this region is fairly complicated by a series of low-level boundaries in the region, including a remnant stationary front/outflow boundary just north of the Wisconsin/Illinois state border and another westward-moving boundary just west of the Chicago Metropolitan area. Although synoptic forcing for ascent is negligible across the area, continued convergence along these surface boundaries amidst a moderately unstable and weakly capped airmass may foster additional isolated development in an environment marginally supportive of updraft rotation. Hail and isolated wind gusts will be the primary threat with this activity, although an isolated tornado cannot be completely ruled out especially with any brief updraft/boundary interaction. Convective coverage is the primary uncertainty with regard to weather watch issuance over the next 1-2 hours in advance of an organizing linear complex over north-central Iowa that should reach the discussion area after about 00-01Z.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Thunderstorms will likely move northeastward into the discussion area from northwestern KS. Isolated large hail/localized severe gusts will be the initial threats. The severe risk may transition to primarily scattered strong/severe gusts later this evening.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Subjective surface analysis places a stationary frontal zone near the Platte River in south-central NE. Radar mosaic early this evening shows intensifying severe thunderstorms near the I-70 corridor in western KS/eastern CO. This activity is forecast to move downstream into the northern periphery of severe thunderstorm watch 213 and eventually into south-central NE this evening as a southerly LLJ strengthens to 50-kt across the central Great Plains. RAP model soundings depict very steep 700-500 mb lapse rates (8 degrees C/km). The KUEX 88-D VAD shows strengthening and veering flow with height in the lowest 2-km which is surmounted by 40-kt 500-mb flow---yielding 40-kt 0-6 km shear. As low-level moisture gradually increases this evening on the nose of the LLJ, diurnal cooling will be slowed and large buoyancy will be maintained. Short-term models indicate scattered strong/severe gusts may evolve with mature convection later this evening from rather efficient downdrafts owing to the very steep lapse rate environment. As a result, a transition from a large hail/wind threat to primarily a wind risk is anticipated during the late evening hours.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Ongoing severe hail/wind threat should reach the eastern portions of WW 214 around 01-02Z. A downstream severe thunderstorm watch will be needed around or before 01Z. Additional redevelopment may occur in western portions of the watch that would pose a hail threat.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Broken linear segments have evolved over north-central and northeastern Iowa, with a series of significant hail and wind reports primarily owing to hybrid bowing/supercell structures in the region. The convection is propagating eastward at around 30-35 knots along a remnant outflow/stationary boundary, with a moderately unstable pre-convective airmass and sufficient vertical wind shear favoring continued organization and a severe threat (potentially significant in localized areas) extending east into southern Wisconsin and northern Illinois. A downstream severe thunderstorm watch is being considered in these areas and will be coordinated soon with affected local forecast offices. Farther west, short-term/high-resolution models continue to suggest redevelopment of convection in southern Minnesota and northern Iowa on the nose of a strengthening low-level jet. Steep mid-level lapse rates will aid in fostering a severe hail threat with this activity when it develops and some potential exists for this activity to develop in western portions of WW 214. For this reason, the severe threat across the entirety of the WW continues.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: The severe threat continues across the entire watch area.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Scattered thunderstorms have developed within an upslope flow regime over WW 215. These storms have occasionally exhibited supercellular characteristics, with several instances of 1-2" hail being reported in the strongest and most persistent activity. Low-level shear is relatively weak, which should keep the overall tornado threat at a minimum. But sufficient deep shear, along with steep mid-level lapse rates and moderate instability, should result in a continued threat for scattered severe hail and isolated instances of damaging wind gusts in and near the WW area through the scheduled 0600 UTC expiration time.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: An additional severe thunderstorm watch may need to be considered for parts of eastern and northeast NE in a couple of hours. The mesoscale environment will become increasingly favorable for severe gust potential. Convective trends will be monitored.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: 00Z surface analysis places a gradient of richer low-level moisture over south-central NE eastward into southeast NE with dewpoints south of the gradient in the 64-68 degrees F range over southeast NE and north-central KS. The 00Z TOP raob sampled a 12.6 g/kg lowest 100-mb mean mixing ratio compared to the drier 9.7 g/kg mixing ratio by the OAX raob. Other than the TOP raob displaying a stronger capping inversion around 800-mb, both raobs exhibited a similar temperature profile from the surface through 500-mb. The OAX raob possessed a 700-500 mb lapse rates of 8.8 degrees C/km. Strong deep-layer shear will support storm organization with the storm cluster along the NE/KS border as it moves east-northeast this evening. It is likely this activity maintains a severe risk into the Grand Island vicinity in a few hours coincident with a strengthening LLJ. The steep lapse rates, increasing low-level moisture, and strong deep shear may support the risk for severe gusts into the late evening and early overnight as storms track east-northeast along the residual baroclinic zone from earlier today.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Recent trends suggest that initiation of new convection is underway across southern Minnesota. Hail will be the primary threat with this activity. A WW is being considered for the region.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Models/observations suggest that intensification of the low-level jet is underway in portions of eastern Nebraska and western Iowa. Convergence along the nose of this low-level jet has led to a few attempts at convective initiation over far southern Minnesota in the past hour. This initiation process is expected to continue with time owing to sustained convergence by the jet and steep mid-level lapse rates (near 9 deg C/km as evidenced on the 00 UTC Omaha, NE RAOB). Given the elevated nature of the expected convection, a hail threat will emerge with strongest, most persistent convection in the region. A severe thunderstorm watch may be required before 10pm local time, although concerns about overall convective coverage may serve as a limiting factor for the overall severe threat. Convective trends will continue to be monitored.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: A lingering severe wind threat will exist with the forward propagating linear segment across the discussion area.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: A line of convection with a history of significant wind and hail reports continues to move eastward at around 35-45 knots across south-central Wisconsin and adjacent northern Illinois. Enough residing shear and instability exists for a continued damaging wind threat with this activity, especially in northern Illinois and far southern Wisconsin where some surface-based instability remains. A southeastward spatial extension of the watch should be considered, especially if additional development occurs on the southern flank of the ongoing convective line over the next hour.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: An isolated hail/wind threat will likely persist across the discussion area over the next couple of hours.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Satellite/lightning imagery indicate continued, yet widely spaced clusters of thunderstorms ongoing across the remaining portions of the WW at this time, with redevelopment noted in northeastern Wyoming. Despite cooling surface temperatures, objective analyses suggest 500-1500 J/kg of MUCAPE in the region, likely as a result of continued steep lapse rates (where the airmass hasn't been convectively overturned) above 40s to 50s F dewpoints. Despite an apparent downward turn in convection over the past hour or so, continued forcing for ascent (in the form of a shortwave indicated over southwestern Wyoming on IR imagery advancing toward the region) will support continued convective clusters with isolated instances of hail and wind gusts over the next couple of hours.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Though some threat for mainly hail persists, overall threat is becoming increasingly marginal. Severe thunderstorm watch 218 is scheduled to expire at 08Z, and no additional WW is expected.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Storms will continue within zone of isentropic ascent north of warm front from southeast South Dakota through southern Minnesota and western Wisconsin supported by a strengthening low-level jet and a northeast-advancing shortwave trough. Other storms are developing along an eastward-moving outflow boundary over a portion of western Iowa. Tendency has been for temperatures in the 800-700 mb layer to gradually warm which has resulted in stronger convective inhibition for parcels originating at or below 850 mb. This suggests updrafts are probably rooted in layers above 800 mb where lower theta-e air is resulting in weaker updrafts. Though mid-level lapse rates and MUCAPE are sufficient to support marginally severe hail, overall threat appears limited. ..Dial.. 05/16/2017 ...Please see www.spc.noaa.gov for graphic product...
